intended_object: The j-th column of a Young diagram μ: the set of cells (i, j) of μ that have column index j. This comes from the docstring and from the module's English-notation convention, where a cell (i, j) is in row i and column j.
explanation: The module uses English notation, where a cell (i, j) sits in row i and column j. In the same file, `row` is defined as the cells whose first coordinate is i. Filtering `μ.cells` by `c.snd = j` therefore gives exactly the cells in column j, as a `Finset`. If column j contains no cells of μ, the result is the empty set, which is correct. The setting is already the general one for Young diagrams, so the definition is not too narrow. There is no separate, more general version of this in Mathlib, because this declaration is Mathlib's own definition.
